episodes.193240: Another afternoon of isolated thunderstorms developed under very hot conditions and an approaching weak short wave trough. A cold front moved through the Texas Panhandle and stalled out from the western South Plains into the extreme southeastern Texas Panhandle. Thunderstorms initially developed along this boundary but with very dry sub-cloud layers, these thunderstorms were efficient strong wind producers. Several storms generated severe wind gusts including a wet microburst near Flomot (Motley County) producing a wind gust of 90 mph.
episodes.193265: Scattered thunderstorms erupted during the mid afternoon hours in north central Alabama, which moved southeast and formed into a broken line of strong to severe thunderstorms into the late afternoon hours across northeastern Alabama.  Some of the thunderstorms became severe, producing damaging wind and small hail. Portions of Dekalb county were hit the hardest with fairly widespread damaging winds near and north of the Fort Payne area.
episodes.193276: Scattered thunderstorms developed along a boundary over northeast Oklahoma and southeast Kansas during the afternoon hours on August 15, 2024. As the boundary progressed, additional thunderstorms developed just north of and along Interstate 44, with hail sizes ranging between quarter size and golf ball size in Dallas and Webster counties, and up to 3.25 inches in Camden County. Additionally, Damaging winds resulted in multiple reports of tree and powerline damage, with 60 mph winds reported in Greene County and 65 mph winds in Miller County. These storms remained over the Missouri Ozarks into the early morning of August 16, 2024, resulting in additional flooding concerns.
episodes.193277: Scattered thunderstorms developed along a boundary over northeast Oklahoma and southeast Kansas on August 15, 2024, with thunderstorms developing just north of and along Interstate 44 by the evening. These storms persisted into the early morning hours of August 16, 2024, resulting in heavy rainfall measuring between 3.25 and 5.49 inches primarily east of Highway 65 in Webster, Wright, Howell, and Texas counties. Flash flooding occurred at multiple locations in Webster County, with areal flooding in Ozark, Douglas, and Texas counties. As the early morning hours progressed, these storms continued to push southeast out of the area by sunrise.||Later in the day, an east to west oriented frontal boundary stalled across south-central Kansas and Missouri, resulting in enough instability and deep layer shear for storms to initiate over Kansas during the early afternoon and push into southeast Kansas by the evening. As the storms moved into southwest Missouri, damaging winds up to 70 mph resulted in numerous reports of trees down in Newton, McDonald, Barry, and Taney counties.
episodes.193290: A third consecutive afternoon of isolated thunderstorms developed across the region. Very hot temperatures allowed storms to initially develop in the central and southern Texas Panhandle and slowly move southeastward. A dry sub-cloud layer allowed these storms to produce strong wind gusts as the surface. Some of these isolated storms became severe with several Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet sites recording severe wind gusts. A wake low developed within the stratiform region of departing thunderstorms and generated a severe wind gust of 59 mph near Friona (Parmer County) measured by the Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet.
episodes.193375: A period of northwest flow persisted across Central Alabama for a few days in mid-August, with a ridge over the southwestern United States and an upper low over the Great Lakes. A storm in Cherokee County produced damage on August 16, and storms the next day produced damage across central and eastern counties. On August 18, numerous thunderstorms passed through central and southern counties in Central Alabama, producing widespread tree damage and several instances of hail. A couple areas in Coosa and Tallapoosa counties saw hail up to golf ball size.
episodes.193591: A line of thunderstorms developed ahead of an advancing cold front during the late night of August 15th/very early morning hours of August 16th. A discrete storm ahead of the line produced a downburst in south central Illinois. A few hours later this same activity produced wind damage in southwest Illinois.
episodes.193710: Two Bering Sea low pressure systems tracked into Western Alaska from August 15 through 18th bringing a period of nearly-persistent southerly winds which led to storm surge and coastal flooding along the Kuskokwim Delta coast and backed up flow along the lower Kuskokwim River. Abundant moisture drawn from the tropical West Pacific by both lows squeezed out moderate to heavy rain in Southwest Alaska, which exacerbated flooding issues along the Kuskokwim River. Flooding was most severe on August 18 as the second low began to enter the Bering Strait, bringing the strongest push of south to southwesterly onshore winds. Coastal communities experienced high water levels which inundated boardwalks, flooded subsistence structures, toppled fuel tanks, damaged ATVs and snowmobiles, and affected the foundations of homes. Along the Kuskokwim River, roads were inundated and closed and at least two houses were flooded in the community of Tuntutuliak.
episodes.193868: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed across central and east-central Wisconsin near a semi-stationary boundary during the early afternoon hours on Friday (8/16).  The strongest storm produced damaging winds across central Wisconsin.
episodes.194230: Late in the evening of August 15th, an area of storms moved through southeast Iowa and west central Illinois. These brought large hail and damaging winds to portions of the area, along with heavy rainfall.
episodes.194231: Late in the evening of August 15th, an area of storms moved through southeast Iowa and west central Illinois. These brought large hail and damaging winds to portions of the area, along with heavy rainfall.
episodes.194431: As a closed upper system strengthened and moved towards the Corn Belt, a trailing cold front pushed into portions of western and central Oklahoma during the afternoon and evening of the 15th. Multiple areas of convective activity emerged near and ahead of this feature, coincident with strong surface heating. Marginal deep-layer wind shear promoted generally disorganized (multi-cell) storm modes. In addition to wind damage (downburst) events, a few reports of large hail were also received.
episodes.194432: A remnant quasi-stationary boundary remained across portions of northern Oklahoma during the day on the 16th. Widely scattered diurnal convection emerged across the aforementioned area. Similar to the 15th (see separate entry), multi-cell thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts and a few reports of hail across portions of western into northern Oklahoma.
episodes.194502: Thunderstorms developed before sunrise and produced a 58 mph wind gust at Goodland and penny size hail in Rawlins County.
episodes.194589: A line of mostly sub-severe thunderstorms produced several instances of damage to power lines around Streator as well as localized flooding in Gibson City late during the night of the 15th.
episodes.194598: Persistent thunderstorms produced flash flooding and nearly 5 inches of rain in the Sheboygan area as low pressure slowly moved through the area.
episodes.195205: A line of marginally severe thunderstorms across northern Illinois remained strong as they moved over Lake Michigan during the evening of the 16th.
episodes.195413: Isolated late afternoon storms morphed into a fairly small mesoscale convective system that surged southeastward through Southwestern Illinois. MLCAPE was 3000 J/kg, decreasing to 2000 J/kg for the evening. Effective bulk shear was 30 kts. A localized swath of significant wind damage occurred in portions of Southwestern Illinois with the most concentrated area of wind damage near Karnak. Other areas receiving wind damage were Gorham, Dongola, Cypress, and Joppa.
episodes.195414: A fairly small and weakening mesoscale convective system surged southeastward into far Western Kentucky during the evening hours of the 15th. MLCAPE was 2000 J/kg for the evening while effective bulk shear was 30 kts. Wind damage was observed in far northeastern Ballard County and western McCracken County.
episodes.195440: Scattered strong to severe storms impacted much of south central and southeast Kansas during the evening hours of August 16th. This activity last until the early morning hours of August 17. The strongest of these storms produced up to baseball sized hail in Cowley County and up to 80 mph winds in Montgomery County.
episodes.195461: A fairly typical summertime upper level pattern was in place with strong high pressure centered well west of the local area. That put southern Louisiana on the eastern periphery of this ridge in a region of northwestern upper level flow. That setup is often conducive for strong to severe thunderstorm development and what took place on August 15th. Thunderstorms initially developed in central Mississippi early afternoon. As the storms traveled southwestward, they moved into an environment with ample instability from strong daytime heating. The resultant cluster of storms organized into a line of strong to severe thunderstorms.
episodes.195462: Thunderstorms for this event initially developed along a sea breeze boundary along the Mississippi coast. One storm on the east side of the Pearl River, began to propagate westward, possibly due to slightly more instability on the western side of the storm created by increased low level moisture typically found in river basins. The thunderstorm reached severe limits as it moved across Washington Parish, producing wind damage across the parish.
episodes.195478: High pressure was over Texas in tandem with northwesterly flow on the east side of the high brought a disturbance through Arkansas leading to severe thunderstorms that tracked from northwest to southeast across the state. At the surface, a cold front boundary provided a lifting mechanism for the thunderstorms as the boundary moved from north to south across the state.
episodes.195515: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed across portions of northeastern Oklahoma during the evening of the 15th, ahead of an approaching cold front. The atmosphere ahead of the cold front became very unstable during the afternoon and early evening across eastern Oklahoma, which supported severe thunderstorms that produced large hail up to half dollar size and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.195518: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed into northeastern Oklahoma during the afternoon of the 16th, and became more widespread across the area during the evening and overnight hours. The atmosphere became very unstable during the late afternoon over eastern Oklahoma, and deep layer wind shear increased over the region during the evening with the approach of an upper level disturbance. This environment supported severe thunderstorms, including some supercells, that produced large hail up to hen egg size and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.195711: A strong storm developed along the coast and produced high wind gusts.
episodes.195775: Thunderstorm clusters and a couple of better organized Supercells spread southeast across the west central Kansas region on the morning of August 16th. The primary threat observed with these storms was hail, some of which were to the size of golf balls.  The storms began intensifying west of Scott City around 9 am, subsequently exiting the Dodge City County Warning Area around noon.
episodes.195840: Scattered thunderstorms and storm clusters developed over the North Carolina mountains during the late afternoon and evening, with some storms moving out over the foothills during the evening. A few of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts.
episodes.195848: Small upper level impulses help to force a weakly organized mesoscale convective system during the late afternoon into early evening in East Tennessee, generating a few instances of severe straight line wind damage.
episodes.195853: A weak surface boundary moving across South Florida brought ample instability, lift, and moisture advection to provide conditions prime for convection on August 15th. Heavy downpours and localized flooding occurred, with slow-moving storms, as the boundary continued to linger in far southern FL throughout the day on the 16th.
episodes.195892: An area of strong to severe thunderstorms moved through Cochise and Santa Cruz County resulting in a couple of severe threshold wind gusts.
episodes.195913: Scattered showers and storms developed over the region as a short wave passed. One storm become severe.
episodes.195919: A warm front lifted north through the area, spawning scattered showers and a few thunderstorms.  One of these storms managed to become strong enough to produce damaging winds.
episodes.195980: Afternoon and evening showers and thunderstorms developed across the northwest and south central portions of the Texas Panhandle. A few of these storms produced wind gusts in excess of 60mph in the Texas Panhandle.
episodes.196043: A cold front interacting with a highly unstable airmass triggered a line of severe thunderstorms across west-central Illinois during the evening of August 15th.  The storms swept across Knox County, northern Peoria County, and Stark County...producing scattered wind damage and hail as large as quarters.  One cell spawned a brief EF-1 tornado northwest of West Jersey in Stark County.  The tornado caused mainly tree damage before quickly dissipating.
episodes.196090: Several reports of severe weather received.
episodes.196190: An isolated severe thunderstorm developed late in the afternoon on August 16th across Howard County Arkansas where surface temperatures were in the upper 90s to lower 100s F, contributing to 8.5-9.5 C/km boundary-layer lapse rates. As such, an intense and persistent updraft developed within the thunderstorm before becoming outflow dominant, with severe wind gusts initiating along the subsequent outflow boundary. However, deep-layer ascent and shear were weak, so this threat remained very isolated near the core of the storm with a few damaging wind reports across Howard County.
episodes.196214: An upper-level low over the Canadian Maritimes brought a strong jet overhead which provided strong shear to the state of New Hampshire on the afternoon of August 15th.  This allowed for strong to severe thunderstorms to develop from Central New Hampshire that quickly traveled southward into Southern New Hampshire, bringing with it large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.196292: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed across various portions of Mississippi during the afternoons of August 14th, 16th, and 17th. These storms caused scattered wind damage from microbursts.
episodes.196385: At the surface, a low wobbled southeastward from the northwestern Great Lakes to southern Lake Huron during the early evening of the 16th through early evening of the 17th. Simultaneously, the attendant warm front moved northeastward from northern Lake Michigan and central Lake Erie to near the northern shore of Lake Ontario and Upper St. Lawrence River Valley, while the trailing cold front moved eastward from the Upper Mississippi River Valley to central Lake Erie and north-central OH.||Within the warm and moist sector, a cluster of multicell thunderstorms persisted eastward across far-northeast OH and generated isolated straight-line convective wind damage in northern Ashtabula County during the early evening of the 16th. The ambient environment exhibited modest MLCAPE of 500-1000 J/kg, modest effective bulk shear of 20-25 knots, and modestly-steep low-level lapse rates near 7C/km. ||During the afternoon through early evening of the 17th, additional multicell thunderstorms developed and persisted northeastward or eastward across north-central and northeast OH, along and ahead of the cold front. These storms generated isolated severe hail and scattered straight-line convective wind damage. Despite modest MLCAPE of 750-1000 J/kg and effective bulk shear near 25 knots, strong convective wind gusts were aided by a corridor of steep low-level lapse rates of 7.5-8C/km. Torrential rainfall was observed in several locations, with flash flooding reported in and near Ravenna where slow storm motions and repeated thunderstorms impacted the area. Precipitable water values of 1.6-1.75 inches resided in the warm and moist sector.
episodes.198941: At the surface, a low wobbled southeastward from the northwestern Great Lakes to southern Lake Huron during the early evening of the 16th through early evening of the 17th. Simultaneously, the attendant warm front moved northeastward from northern Lake Michigan and central Lake Erie to near the northern shore of Lake Ontario and Upper St. Lawrence River Valley, while the trailing cold front moved eastward from the Upper Mississippi River Valley to central Lake Erie and north-central OH.||Within the warm and moist sector, a cluster of multicell thunderstorms persisted eastward along the shore of far-northeast OH and generated a gale-force peak convective wind gust at Conneaut Breakwater Light during the early evening of the 16th. These storms occurred in an environment with weak MUCAPE and moderate effective bulk shear. During the early afternoon through early evening of the 17th, additional multicell thunderstorms developed and persisted northeastward or eastward over and near the southern shore of Lake Erie, along and ahead of the cold front. These storms generated isolated gale-force peak convective wind gusts amidst moderate MUCAPE and effective bulk shear, respectively.

Nearly-persistent southerly winds led to storm surge and backed up flow, exacerbated by heavy rain, along the Kuskokwim River between August 15 and 18. Residents reported flooding and rapid bank erosion during high tides on August 16 and 17 at Akiak, Napakiak, Kasigluk, and Tuntutuliak. At Napakiak, a village elder reported the bank in front of the school was eroding rapidly and was only about 6 ft from the structure. Water inundated most low spots in the village, including the low spot in the road to the dump. Water levels were reported to be higher than during breakup flooding in May. A resident in Kasigluk reported water encroached on low lying residences, with similar water levels to this year's breakup and only a few inches lower than during Merbok in September 2022. The highest tide levels of the event occurred on August 18 as southerly winds gusted 50-55 mph into the Kuskokwim Delta. In Tuntutuliak, a resident reported that water entered at least two houses. In Bethel, the south boat harbor and East Avenue were closed due to flooding. A National Weather Service employee at the Weather Service Office in Bethel reported waves of 1.5 ft on the Kuskokwim River. In Napakiak, the storm produced localized wind damage to roofing and some smoke houses and subsistence camps were damaged.
